papers.title_in_file: Generative Quantum Data Embeddings for Supervised Learning
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, Section II B (Wasserstein bound) summary text, Section IV Wasserstein discussion, conclusion; appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: An energy-based generative architecture search (EGAS) for quantum data embeddings in kernel-SVM classification, with a Wasserstein-distance bound on attainable gains.

assertions.value: The authors report that EGAS finds embeddings whose kernel-SVM performance matches or exceeds the ZZ and NQE quantum embedding baselines on all evaluated datasets.
quotes: Our empirical results show that EGAS consistently identifies embeddings whose kernel-SVM performance matches or exceeds that of the existing quantum embedding baselines, including ZZ and NQE, across all evaluated datasets.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from the authors' own experiments.
assertions.reader_inference: Results are from kernel simulation on the paper's chosen datasets; no hardware run was seen in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors derive bounds on the achievable empirical risk in terms of the Wasserstein distance in the input space, and state that this gives an a priori diagnostic of datasets where large gains from embedding optimization are unlikely.
quotes: We explain this saturation by deriving bounds on the achievable empirical risk in terms of the Wasserstein distance in the input space
This analysis provides an a priori diagnostic for identifying datasets in which large architecture-dependent gains are unlikely within a fixed embedding family.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derived in Section II B and Appendix B; derivation not independently checked by the reader; the paper notes the bound may be loose.

assertions.value: The authors state that on some datasets the evaluated embeddings give tightly clustered QKSVM accuracies, which they attribute to limited variation in the available search space under the fixed depth and gate-pool setting.
quotes: In other datasets, however, the evaluated embeddings lead to tightly clustered QKSVM accuracies, indicating that the available search space provides only limited variation in classification accuracy under the fixed depth and gate-pool setting considered here.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of scope, Section V.

assertions.value: The authors state that deployment on near-term quantum hardware will require search spaces tailored to hardware-native gate sets and connectivity constraints.
quotes: Finally, deployment on near-term quantum hardware will require search spaces tailored to hardware-native gate sets and connectivity constraints
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of a limit of the present work, Section V.

papers.title_in_file: First quantum machine learning applications on an on-site room-temperature quantum computer
papers.what_it_is: A data re-uploading universal quantum classifier trained on a simulator and run on a two-qubit room-temperature quantum computer (QB-QDK) by Quantum Brilliance.

assertions.value: The authors report classification accuracies of 0.95, 0.97 and 0.873 on an ideal state vector simulator and 0.925, 0.955 and 0.850 on the QB-QDK for three classification problems.
quotes: reaching excellent classification accuracies of 0.95, 0.97, and 0.873 and 0.925, 0.955, and 0.850 on the ideal state vector simulator and the QB-QDK, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Authors are the device vendor reporting their own product's result.
assertions.reader_inference: Authors are Quantum Brilliance staff; the device is their product. Low-dimensional 2D synthetic tasks.

assertions.value: The authors report that no on-device training or noise mitigation was required and that accuracies were only 1.5% to 2.5% lower than ideal state vector simulation.
quotes: (iii) no on-device training or noise mitigation techniques were required to successfully deploy the classically optimised models to the integrated quantum hardware, reaching classification accuracies only 1.5% to 2.5% lower than what is possible with ideal state vector simulators.
assertions.certainty_reason: Vendor's description of its own device result.

assertions.value: The paper states that the deployed models were trained entirely on an ideal state vector simulator and that no noise mitigation was applied to the measured bit counts.
quotes: (i) the deployed models were trained entirely on an ideal state vector simulator, allowing us to directly assess the performance of the QB-QDK against the ideal (noise-free) performance,
(iii) no noise mitigation techniques were applied to the measured bit counts.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that, due to quantum noise, a few central data points were seriously misclassified, and that such effects could lead to problems in time-constrained QML applications.
quotes: Due to quantum noise, a few central data points were seriously misclassified
Such effects could lead to problems in timeconstrained QML applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit.

papers.title_in_file: Probabilistic Pathways: New Frontiers in Quantum Ensemble Control
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, simulation section 5, final comments; derivation sections skimmed
papers.what_it_is: A probabilistic (KL-divergence based) control framework for steering quantum ensembles, with simulation results for spin and lambda-type systems.

assertions.value: The authors propose steering a quantum ensemble by minimizing the discrepancy between the probabilistic description of its dynamics and a desired probabilistic description, and state that this yielded an analytical form for the randomized controller under Gaussian noise.
quotes: The minimisation of the discrepancy between the probabilistic description of the dynamics of a quantum ensemble and a predefined desired probabilistic description is the key step in the proposed framework.

The solution is then demonstrated on a specific case involving quantum systems affected by Gaussian noise and described by Gaussian pdfs, which yielded an analytical form for the randomized controller.
assertions.certainty_reason: Derivation by the authors; not independently checked.
assertions.reader_inference: Quantum control, not a machine-learning workload.

assertions.value: In simulation, the authors report fidelities almost equal to 1 between the target state and the final states of 1000 ensemble members.
quotes: Figure (4) displays the fidelities between the target state and the final states of 1000 ensemble members interacting with the optimal controller. We observe that the fidelities are almost equal to 1
assertions.certainty_reason: Simulation result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that measurement backaction was not explicitly accounted for in the current work.
quotes: While this effect was not explicitly accounted for in the current work, it's an important consideration as it can potentially impact the effectiveness of the control field.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section 6.

papers.title_in_file: Quantum Deep Learning: Sampling Neural Nets with a Quantum Annealer
papers.partial_detail: abstract, background, contributions, scaling and timing, conclusions
papers.what_it_is: Maps a classically trained convolutional neural network onto a quadratic binary model run on a D-Wave quantum annealer for digit classification.

assertions.value: The authors report finding an embedding and obtaining samples from a four layer model of 358 nodes on the D-Wave QPU, and state this was the largest network they could run.
quotes: Using our approach we were able to find an embedding and obtain samples from a four layer model comprising 358 nodes
The largest network we were able run had four layers and 358 nodes.
assertions.certainty_reason: One study on one device.

assertions.value: The authors estimate that classification and printing would take about 8000 microseconds on a classical computer, against 168 microseconds to obtain samples from the QPU, which they say suggests a possible speed up of at least one order of magnitude.
quotes: We repeated the experiment on a classical computer and estimated that classification and printing out would take about 8000 microseconds whereas samples can be obtained from the QPU in 168 microseconds
assertions.certainty_reason: Estimate from one study; the speed up is stated as suggested, not demonstrated end to end.
assertions.reader_inference: The classical figure is an estimate; the paper also notes access and programming overheads are not in the QPU figure.

assertions.value: The authors state that their timing focuses on the annealing time and that access, programming, sampling and postprocessing time overheads currently exist.
quotes: Regarding timings, we have focused on the annealing time
Currently, there are time overheads (access, programming, sampling and postprocessing) involved with this process
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limit, Section 5.

assertions.value: The authors state that the digit experiment used only one randomly chosen digit from each class and one embedding.
quotes: This experiment was performed on only one randomly chosen digit from each class and with one embedding for Q.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of the experiment's scope, Section 4.2.

papers.title_in_file: Battery health prognosis using Physics-informed neural network with Quantum Feature mapping
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, contributions, methodology opening, results discussion, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A physics-informed neural network with a Nystrom-approximated quantum-inspired kernel feature map (QPINN) for battery state-of-health estimation.

assertions.value: The authors report an average SOH estimation accuracy of 99.46% across different datasets, with MAPE and RMSE reductions of up to 65% and 62% against state-of-the-art baselines.
quotes: The proposed method achieves an average SOH estimation accuracy of 99.46% across different datasets, substantially outperforming state-of-the-art baselines, with reductions in MAPE and RMSE of up to 65% and 62%, respectively.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study.

assertions.value: The authors describe their method as a hybrid quantum-inspired and physics-informed framework built on a quantum-inspired kernel-based feature extraction layer.
assertions.anchor: Section I Key Contributions; Section V Conclusion
quotes: Introduced a dedicated quantum-inspired kernel-based feature extraction layer
This work presented QPINN, a hybrid quantum-inspired and physics-informed framework for battery state-of-health (SOH) estimation.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's own statement of what the method is, Section I and V.
assertions.reader_inference: The feature map is a classical Nystrom-approximated kernel; I found no statement of a quantum device run in the sections read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the method was validated on a multi-chemistry dataset of 310,705 samples from 387 cells.
quotes: This method was validated on a large-scale, multi-chemistry dataset of 310,705 samples from 387 cells
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper's statement of its own evaluation setup, Abstract.

assertions.value: The authors state that zero-shot transfer performance remains limited and that the experiments cover four datasets with specific operating ranges, so broader evaluation is necessary to assess generality.
quotes: The model's zero-shot transfer performance remains limited, reflecting the challenges posed by differences in cycling protocols, degradation profiles, and data collection setups.
Finally, the current experiments are conducted on four datasets with specific operating ranges, and broader evaluation is necessary to assess generality.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limits, Section IV B.

papers.title_in_file: Generalization Error in Quantum Machine Learning in the Presence of Sampling Noise
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, numerical comparison, Section IV results, discussion; appendix derivations not read
papers.what_it_is: A statistical-mechanics (replica) calculation of training and generalization errors for quantum reservoir computing with finite data and finite measurement shots.

assertions.value: The authors use statistical-mechanics methods to calculate training and generalization errors of a generic quantum machine learning system with finite training data and finite measurement shots, and state that the findings justify Eigentask Learning as minimizing generalization error.
quotes: we use methodologies from statistical mechanics to calculate the training and generalization errors of a generic quantum machine learning system when the input training dataset and output measurement sampling shots are both finite.
Our analytical findings, supported by numerical validation, offer solid justification that Eigentask Learning provides optimal learning in the sense of minimizing generalization errors.
assertions.certainty_reason: Replica-method result that relies on a large-N saddle-point approximation and a Gaussian approximation; not independently checked.

assertions.value: The authors report that, for a 6-qubit quantum Ising model with a random drive, the empirical training and generalization errors match the replica-theory values well, especially at large N.
quotes: The underlying quantum system is a 6-qubit quantum Ising model with a random drive.
These data match well, especially for the practical large N limit.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical simulation of one system in one study.

assertions.value: The authors state that the analysis works when the eigentask combination coefficients are accurately known, which in practice they are not, and that it considers only the first- and second-order cumulants of input data.
quotes: Third, the analysis in this paper works when accurate values of r(k) in the combination coefficients in eigentasks are known. In practice, those coefficients are unknown
Secondly, both the Eigentask Analysis and replica methods in Ref. [24] only consider the first- and second-order cumulants of input data
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limits, Section V.

papers.title_in_file: Power of data in quantum machine learning
papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, geometric-difference and projected-kernel sections, discussion; appendices not read
papers.what_it_is: Prediction-error bounds for classical and quantum kernel models, a geometric-difference test for quantum advantage, and a projected quantum kernel tested up to 30 qubits on engineered data.

assertions.value: The authors state that, using rigorous prediction error bounds as a foundation, they develop a methodology for assessing potential quantum advantage in learning tasks, and that the bounds are tight asymptotically and empirically predictive for a wide range of learning models.
quotes: Using rigorous prediction error bounds as a foundation, we develop a methodology for assessing potential quantum advantage in learning tasks. The bounds are tight asymptotically and empirically predictive for a wide range of learning models.
assertions.certainty_reason: Bounds derived in the paper (abstract; derivation in the appendices, not re-checked by the reader).

assertions.value: The authors state that they showed quantitatively how classical ML algorithms with data can become computationally more powerful, and that a prediction advantage for quantum models is not guaranteed even if the data come from a quantum process that is challenging to simulate.
quotes: We showed quantitatively how classical ML algorithms with data can become computationally more powerful, and a prediction advantage for quantum models is not guaranteed even if the data comes from a quantum process that is challenging to independently simulate.
assertions.certainty_reason: Combines bounds with numerical tests on a chosen set of models and data sets.

assertions.value: The authors report that on engineered data sets projected quantum kernels outperform all tested classical models in prediction error, in numerical tests up to 30 qubits.
quotes: On engineered data sets, projected quantum kernels outperform all tested classical models in prediction error.
in one of the largest numerical tests for gate-based quantum machine learning to date, up to 30 qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result on data sets engineered by the authors to show a separation.
assertions.reader_inference: The data sets are engineered for maximal separation, not drawn from practical problems.

assertions.value: The authors state that further research is required to find use cases on data sets closer to practical interest, and that additional work is needed to identify embeddings that are hard to approximate classically yet show meaningful signal on local observables for very large numbers of qubits.
quotes: Further research will be required to find use cases on data sets closer to practical interest and evaluate potential claims of advantage

Additional work will be needed to identify embeddings that satisfy the sometimes conflicting requirements of being hard to approximate classically and exhibiting meaningful signal on local observables for very large numbers of qubits.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own stated limits, Discussion.

papers.partial_detail: abstract, introduction, resource comparison, ansatz comparison, conclusion
papers.what_it_is: A variational quantum algorithm (QGOA) that adds message passing inspired by graph neural networks to QAOA-style optimization of QUBO problems, tested in simulation on portfolio and vertex-cover tasks.

assertions.value: The authors state that their QGOA algorithm shows significant improvements for QUBO problems in resource efficiency and solution precision compared to QAOA, its variants, and other quantum graph neural networks.
quotes: which demonstrates significant improvements in performance for solving QUBO problems in terms of resource efficiency and solution precision, compared to QAOA, its variants, and other quantum graph neural networks.
assertions.certainty_reason: Empirical result from one study's numerical experiments.

assertions.value: The authors report that in the range of 4-qubits to 12-qubits, QGOA showed advantages over QAOA in both quantum and classical resources, and state that the advantages become more pronounced as system size grows.
quotes: In the range of 4-qubits to 12-qubits, as shown in Fig. 4, the QGOA method demonstrated significant advantages over the QAOA method in terms of both quantum and classical resources.
These advantages become even more pronounced as the spatial dimension of the system increases.
assertions.certainty_reason: Numerical result from one study; resource counts shown in Figure 4.

assertions.value: The authors state that the ansatz comparison uses numerical experiments on nine qubits-portfolio optimization, and describe their approach as still in its early stages.
quotes: To evaluate the effectiveness of the QGOA method, we conduct several numerical experiments with different methods in nine qubits-portfolio optimization.
While our approach is still in its early stages, we believe that it represents an important step
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors' own statement of setup and maturity, Sections VI and VII.
